Backyard sports turf beside three golf courses

Sports and fitness turf in Reunion, a bocce court, a home-gym sled track or a small fitness pad, is quoted per job rather than a single price range, since layout and product vary more than a lawn does. It's a genuinely small market in a community where golf already dominates the athletic identity of the place.

Reviewed by Luis Austin, owner · Last reviewed September 21, 2026

Golf already owns the sports conversation here

With three championship courses running past 6,900 yards each on the same property reunionresort.com, a Reunion homeowner looking for a competitive outlet in the yard is a rarer request than in a community without that kind of golf already built in. The backyard sports turf we do install in Reunion tends to be a fitness accessory, a sled track for a home gym or a small putting-adjacent chipping pad, rather than a full court or field.

Why is standing water worse on a court than on a lawn?

A backing built to drain faster than thirty inches of water an hour matters on an outdoor Reunion bocce court or a backyard soccer patch for a more immediate reason than it does on a plain lawn: a puddle that a family might just walk around on open grass sits directly in the path of a rolling ball or a running cut on a dedicated sports surface. The same permeable backing and washed-rock base used anywhere else on the lot clears that water quickly enough that a court is playable again shortly after a Central Florida afternoon storm passes.

Say you want a sled track along a side yard

Say you have a 6-by-40-foot side strip beside a Reunion home, about 240 sq ft, that isn't wide enough for much else and gets quoted for a home-gym sled track. Because the base needs to handle a loaded sled dragged back and forth rather than just foot traffic, the build uses a denser compaction pass and a low-pile, high-durability turf glued at the edges rather than staked, and the whole job is priced from a site visit rather than a published per-foot number given how specialized the wear pattern is. A strip this size and shape usually clears association review faster than a highly visible backyard project, since it sits along a side fence line rather than facing the street or a golf course.

What actually gets built when it does

A home-gym sled track needs a firm, low-pile turf glued or nailed flat over a compacted base, built to handle a weighted sled dragged repeatedly across the same strip rather than foot traffic alone, which is a different wear pattern than any lawn sees. A backyard bocce court, less common but not unheard of on a larger Reunion lot, needs a level, contained bed with edging tight enough to keep the playing surface true.

Is an hour of bocce a longer heat exposure than crossing a yard?

Full summer sun pushes outdoor turf to 120 to 150°F, and a plain yard crossing exposes bare feet or paws to that for only a few seconds at a time, but a full bocce match or a pickup soccer game on a Reunion court keeps players standing and moving across the same hot surface for the better part of an hour. A rinse before play drops that temperature 30 to 50 degrees, which matters more here since the exposure is sustained rather than brief. Scheduling matches for morning or evening in peak summer avoids the worst of it without changing anything about the court itself.

Working post footings into a batting cage's base plan

A batting cage's netting frame needs its corner and mid-span posts set into their own footings within the same base a Reunion yard's turf sits on, and those footings have to go in before the surrounding washed rock gets compacted around them, not after. Loose fill packed in close to a footing after the fact settles unevenly over time and can let a post lean, which slackens the netting it holds. Planning footing locations against the base layout at the start keeps the compacted rock and the posts settling together rather than working against each other later.

Space is the real constraint on a Reunion lot

Between the pool, the screened lanai and whatever landscaping the association expects to see, many Reunion backyards simply don't have the open run of flat ground a sports surface needs, which is the practical reason this stays a small category here regardless of interest. A sled track fits into a narrow side strip where a bocce court usually can't.

Does turf installation have to wait on a separate netting contractor?

When a batting cage's posts and netting come from a specialist rather than our own crew, the Reunion turf schedule has to work around whoever sets that frame, since turf edging and seam placement depend on exactly where the posts land. Finishing turf before the frame is set risks trimming and re-trimming around posts that move slightly once the netting installer actually anchors them; waiting until the frame is confirmed and locked in place keeps the turf's final cuts from needing a second pass once both crews are done.

Why infill depth on a court is a performance check, not just upkeep

Checking infill depth on a Reunion bocce court or agility strip is less about appearance and more about how the surface actually plays, since a thin patch changes how a ball rolls or how a foot grips during a hard cut well before it looks visibly bare to the eye. Running a hand across the pile in a few spots along the run catches an uneven depth sooner than a visual glance would, and topping off just the thin section keeps the whole surface behaving consistently rather than waiting until play itself starts to feel different.

Questions people ask

Is a backyard sports court realistic on a typical Reunion lot?

Rarely for a full court. Most Reunion lots are sized around the pool, lanai and landscaping the association expects, leaving room for a narrow feature like a sled track more often than a full-size court or field.

Does sports turf need a different base than a lawn?

Usually a denser compaction and sometimes a firmer product, since it's built to handle repeated, concentrated wear in one spot rather than distributed foot traffic; see the sports and fitness turf page for the range of builds we quote.
